title: When the Bridge Breaks
premise: In the final year of the Great War, Petra Whitlock keeps a secret ledger of soldiers' true names and fates — the ones the officers' reports omit. When a sealed letter from a dying colonel names her late father's family as silent partners in a scheme to sell forged medical exemptions, Petra is drawn into the Whitlock household she never knew, where every member's fortune rests on the lie. As the armistice approaches, she must expose the plot without destroying the half-sister who befriended her, and in the end she chooses to give the last berth on the final hospital ship home not to the innocent heir but to the guilty brother who confessed, sending him to face justice alive while she stays to keep the ledger — and the truth — in her own hands.
about_author: Jonah Dunmore is the pen name of a former military archivist who spent a decade cataloguing field hospital records from the Western Front. He writes historical fiction about the paper trails wars leave behind and the people brave enough to read them.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Omitted Names
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At a casualty clearing station in 1918, Petra records the names officers strike from official reports — deserters, the shell-shocked, the wrongly declared dead. When a dying colonel presses a sealed letter into her hands and whispers her surname, Whitlock, she realizes her own family name is written inside. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath professional composure.

chapters.title: A Letter with Wax and Weight
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Unable to sleep, she reads the colonel's letter: the Whitlock family has profited for two years from forged exemption papers, and he wants the scheme exposed before the armistice buries it. She burns nothing and tells no one. Emotional beat: the first crack in her loyalty to a family she's never met.

chapters.title: Leave to Ashford
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Granted emergency leave, she travels to the Kent estate where the Whitlocks live — the father who abandoned her mother, the half-siblings she's only imagined. She arrives posing as a nurse seeking work with the family's convalescent ward. Emotional beat: hope curdling into impostor's guilt.

chapters.title: The House That Paid for Itself
chapters.summary: Marian Whitlock's POV. The half-sister, sharp and warm, tours Petra through a house conspicuously renewed — new roofs, a private ambulance, imported coal. Marian defends the family's good fortune with practiced ease. Emotional beat: affection offered freely, which makes deception feel like theft.

chapters.title: Brother Edmund's Ledgers
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra gains access to the estate office under pretense of filing medical records and finds account entries matching the colonel's letter — payments routed through a London solicitor. Edmund, the eldest son, catches her and watches her too long. Emotional beat: the hunter realizing she may be the hunted.

chapters.title: Dinner with Ghosts
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Over dinner, Edmund probes the new nurse's origins while his father toasts the family's service record. Petra answers every question with a truth that conceals the truth. Edmund suspects but says nothing — yet. Emotional beat: a duel fought entirely in courtesies.

chapters.title: What the Groundskeeper Saw
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The old groundskeeper, once her father's friend, recognizes her mother's face in hers and tells her how the family bought silence after a worker's death was blamed on a forged-exemption soldier sent back to the front. Emotional beat: grief for a father she is only now meeting through his sins.

chapters.title: Marian's Confidences
chapters.summary: Marian's POV. Marian confesses to Petra that she suspects the money isn't clean but has chosen not to know, because knowing would cost her the hospital ward she runs for wounded locals. Emotional beat: the terrible comfort of willful blindness, offered as friendship.

chapters.title: The Solicitor's Clerk
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra travels to London, traces the solicitor's clerk, and trades a name from her ledger for a copy of the exemption-forger's contract. The signature authorizing payments is her father's. Emotional beat: evidence secured, but at the price of burning a bridge she may need.

chapters.title: Edmund Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund confronts Petra privately — he has learned who she is — and offers her a place in the family and a share of the quiet money if she burns the colonel's letter. Emotional beat: temptation dressed as belonging; the first time the family feels like it could be hers.

chapters.title: The Berth List
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. News arrives: one berth remains on the last hospital ship before the armistice, and the family must choose who goes to London — the ailing father, the fragile younger brother Thomas, or Marian, whose ward could burn with the scandal. Petra is asked to advise, as a medical professional. Emotional beat: the plot's moral fulcrum placed in her hands.

chapters.title: Thomas in the Orchard
chapters.summary: Thomas's POV. The youngest Whitlock, discharged with wounds no one discusses, tells Petra he knows what the money bought — he carried the forged papers to men at the front and has counted the graves since. Emotional beat: a conscience already broken, asking her for a punishment he can't ask for himself.

chapters.title: The Father's Room
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra finally faces her father, who admits everything and asks only that the name Whitlock survive intact. He offers her the one thing she came for — acknowledgment — in exchange for silence. Emotional beat: the inheritance she wanted is a debt she never agreed to.

chapters.title: Armistice Rumors
chapters.summary: Marian's POV. Rumors of peace sweep the county; the household celebrates while Marian finds the forged contract in Petra's room and must decide what kind of sister she wants to be. Emotional beat: betrayal and recognition arriving in the same hour.

chapters.title: The Choice of Berths
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra recommends Thomas for the berth — publicly, on medical grounds. Privately, she has arranged with the ship's matron that Thomas will be delivered to military authorities in London, where he has asked to confess. Emotional beat: justice disguised as mercy, and mercy disguised as exile.

chapters.title: Edmund's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund discovers the arrangement and moves to send his father instead, planning to pin the scheme on the dead colonel. He burns the solicitor's copy — but not the original, which he cannot find. Emotional beat: a man protecting a family that no longer exists.

chapters.title: What Petra Kept
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Revealed: Petra has held the colonel's original letter and her ledger all along; she sends copies to the War Office and a London newspaper the night before the armistice is signed. Emotional beat: the quiet violence of paper, wielded by the person everyone underestimated.

chapters.title: The Eleventh Hour
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, interwoven. As church bells announce the armistice, the household shatters: the father collapses, Edmund flees toward the coast, Marian reads the morning's evidence aloud to the staff rather than hide it. Emotional beat: peace arriving as an avalanche.

chapters.title: The Last Berth Sails
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the dock, Petra sees Thomas aboard the ship, bound for confession and a shortened sentence she has bargained for with her testimony. Edmund is taken at Dover. Emotional beat: the cost of the choice made visible — she saved the guilty one and sent him to justice alive.

chapters.title: Marian's Verdict
chapters.summary: Marian's POV. Marian confronts Petra: she understands the choice, may even forgive it, but cannot call her sister. She keeps the convalescent ward, funded now by the estate's honest remainder. Emotional beat: love that survives truth but not trust — a truce, not a reunion.

chapters.title: The Inquest
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the military inquiry, Petra testifies with her ledger open, naming every omitted man and every purchased silence, including her father's. The Whitlock name is stripped of its honors; she feels neither triumph nor relief, only the weight of having said it all aloud. Emotional beat: justice achieved outside the law's comfort, at the price of every easy silence.

chapters.title: A New Page in the Ledger
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra returns to nursing in a demobilized France, her ledger now a public record and her hands free of it. She begins a new book — not of omissions, but of the names she helped bring home. Emotional beat: hard-won peace; the inheritance she finally claims is the truth itself.
